text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** NMC only makes sense if weight is your top priority and you'll use the unit rarely.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, against roughly 500-1,000 for most NMC units. At one full cycle a day, that's about 8+ years versus under 2. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/))
- **Safety:** No lithium battery is risk-free, but in lab tests LFP cells failed more mildly. One test had the LFP cell peak at 259°C versus 731°C for NMC. LFP also tends to produce smoke rather than flames. That matters if the unit sits indoors or in a vehicle. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/))
- **Cost:** The price gap has largely closed. One retailer database shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC, so LFP is much cheaper per rated cycle. ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap is smaller, about 10-16% per pound in two datasets. The case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. Some LFP models even beat some NMC ones. For example, the Anker SOLIX C1000 (LFP) holds 37.1 Wh/lb versus 26.1 for the Goal Zero Yeti 1000 (NMC). ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))

**Caveats**
- **Cycle ratings aren't directly comparable.** Some brands rate to 70% capacity and others to 80%, and test conditions differ. Check which one a listing uses.
- **Cold weather is a wash.** Most stations of either chemistry won't charge below 32°F, so check the specific manual. One source claims LFP is much better in the cold, but others found the limits depend on the maker, not the chemistry.
- **Occasional use narrows the gap.** If you only use it a few times a year, calendar aging will matter more than cycle count.
- **Fit comes first.** Make sure the output and capacity can run your devices before you worry about chemistry.

**Examples to compare** (affiliate links, per the source; the prices and codes are from Dealectric's testing on Oct 21-24, 2026 and may change):
- **LFP, longest life:** [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). It has 2,073.6 Wh, is rated for 6,000+ cycles to 80%, and costs $899.
- **LFP, mid-size:** [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). It has 1,152 Wh, is rated for 3,500+ cycles, and costs $499 for the station alone.
- **LFP, budget and light:** [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh). It has 1,024 Wh and weighs about 13 kg. Its 3,000-cycle rating is only to 70%, and the listing has some contradictory specs.
- **NMC, weight-focused:** [ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-1451wh). It has 1,451 Wh in about 13 kg and is rated for 2,500+ cycles. It costs $664, and the code EXTRA10 reportedly brings it to $597.60. Sources disagree on its solar input (1,000 W versus 650 W).

Tell me your intended use (home backup, camping, van, CPAP) and budget, and I can narrow this down.
